result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps within a dense commercial environment. However, pedestrian safety is compromised by significant visual obstructions from large vehicles and multiple lanes of traffic that increase exposure during crossing.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Large Vehicles
hazards.description: A large delivery truck and passenger vehicle are positioned close to the crosswalk, severely limiting sightlines between pedestrians and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Multi-lane Exposure
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic, including a dedicated transit lane, increasing the risk of multiple-threat crashes.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking or standing zones at least 20 feet before the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines between motorists and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and place pedestrians in a more visible position before they enter the roadway.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signal to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before the parallel vehicle traffic gets a green light.

result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with high-visibility crosswalks and pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the multi-lane roadway creates a long crossing distance without a median refuge.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple lanes of traffic without a mid-point refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection across the main roadway

hazards.name: Potential Turning Conflicts
hazards.description: Vehicles turning right or left at the signalized intersection may conflict with pedestrians in the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program the traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban intersection with wide sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and pedestrian signals. While basic infrastructure is present, the presence of large stopped vehicles near the crossing creates potential sightline issues for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Large vehicles stopped near the intersection corner block the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, along the curb where the white van is parked.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Implement 'no standing' zones near the intersection to clear sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and physically prevent vehicles from blocking sightlines at the corner.

result.summary: The image shows a dense urban commercial environment with wide sidewalks and a marked continental crosswalk. However, pedestrians face a long crossing distance across multiple lanes of traffic, and a vehicle stopped near the crosswalk creates a significant visual obstruction.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Stopped Vehicle
hazards.description: A white SUV is stopped immediately adjacent to the crosswalk, blocking the sightlines between pedestrians entering the roadway and oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
